description:
Scope: planning only for lib/zaq/channels/delivery_confirmation.ex lines 34 and 37. No production change, external service, UI/E2E, database, or new test seam. Existing test/zaq/channels/api_test.exs already covers confirmed success, Engine error fallback and unconfirmed provider error; reuse existing Zaq.NodeRouterMock defined in test/support/mocks.ex against Zaq.NodeRouter.Behaviour. Exact exclusive test path to add: test/zaq/channels/delivery_confirmation_test.exs. Do not modify api_test.exs or share edits with another coverage task.

Test-first steps:
1. Add Zaq.Channels.DeliveryConfirmationTest with use ExUnit.Case, async: true; import Mox; setup :verify_on_exit!; alias Zaq.Channels.DeliveryConfirmation, Zaq.Engine.Messages.Outgoing and Zaq.Event. No DB setup needed. Build one small confirmed receipt %{confirmation: :confirmed, message_id: "external-1"}, and one %Outgoing{body: "delivered", metadata: %{user_message_id: "u-1", assistant_message_id: "a-1", trace: "private"}}; pass delivery_node_router: Zaq.NodeRouterMock through record/3, never alter global config or Mox mode.
2. Line 34 (rescue): expect NodeRouterMock.dispatch/1 once with %Event{request: %{receipt: ^receipt, outgoing: routed}, opts: opts}; assert event destination is :engine via its documented Event field (check struct), opts[:action] == :record_delivery_confirmation, routed.body and both allowed metadata IDs match and :trace is absent. Raise a deterministic RuntimeError in callback. Assert record({:ok, receipt}, outgoing, opts) == {:ok, Map.put(receipt, :confirmation_recording, :unavailable)}; assert input receipt is unchanged and not reclassified as failed delivery. Expectation plus verify_on_exit! proves one dispatch, not a silent pre-dispatch failure.
3. Line 37 (catch): use same fixture and process-private expectation but exit(:engine_unavailable) in dispatch/1, not a raised exception or a killed spawned process. Assert identical confirmed receipt with confirmation_recording: :unavailable, receipt identity preserved and expectation met. This specifically exercises catch :exit rather than rescue; assert test process remains alive implicitly through completion.
4. Optional focused control in same file: non-confirmed response passes through unchanged and router receives no dispatch (existing API coverage may suffice). Avoid redundant success/failure cases already in api_test.exs.

Isolation and mocks: existing behavior-backed Mox boundary, per-test process-private expectations only; no new mock modules or helpers beyond a local fixture function if duplication warrants it; no application env, process dictionary, timers, sleeps, child processes or SQL Sandbox. No Mox.allow/3 necessary. Property assessment: these are two discrete exception classes and a fixed fallback mapping; no broad input space, normalization or invariant requiring StreamData here. Existing paths cover routing semantics. If Event struct field names differ, inspect Event.new/3 and use exact supported destination field; no production edits solely for coverage. If the Mox dispatch cannot inject the failure or coverage reports a different source mapping, document concrete blocker and report rather than inventing dead-code assertions.

Validation after implementation (not in this planning task): run mix test test/zaq/channels/delivery_confirmation_test.exs in isolation, then mix q through Context Mode; verify fresh coverage report attributes execution to lines 34 and 37 (coverage phase via mix coveralls.json then mix coverup after successful report per workflow), inspect diff for test-only scope. Final mix precommit gate only at final human-approval stage. No feature E2E: pure channel-to-engine error-handling contract, no UX. Action reuse: not applicable, tests exercise existing record/3 and dispatch/1 and add no operation or tool. Blockers: none known; no unreachable branch expected because dispatch can raise and exit synchronously.
title: [coverage] Cover DeliveryConfirmation rescue and exit fallback
